chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sajistani told me, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzaymah narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Hijr narrated to us, Hijr narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamar, from Rubay ibn Kharash, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

A servant does not believe until he believes in four things: until he bears witness that there is no god but God, alone, without a partner, and that I am the Messenger of God, sent by Him with the truth, and until he believes in the resurrection after death, and until he believes in the divine decree.

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but God (Declaration of Monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What are the four conditions for true faith in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* establishes the foundational pillars of faith (Usul al-Din) within the Shia tradition, linking the declaration of monotheism and prophethood with the eschatological concepts of resurrection and divine decree. It reflects the early scholarly consensus that true belief requires not just verbal affirmation but internal conviction in God's absolute unity, the truth of Muhammad's mission, the reality of the afterlife, and the predestination of all affairs by God.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-8 Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sejezy narrated that Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khozaymeh quoted Ali ibn Hijr, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Mansoor ibn al-Moe’tamar, on the authority of Rub’ay ibn Kharash, on the authority of Ali (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “

One is not a true believer unless he does the following four things: bears witness to the fact that ‘There is no god but God, He is One and there are no partners for Him, and I (Muhammad) am God’s Prophet; I have been rightly appointed; there is resurrection after death; and there is destiny.’”
